title: Unauthenticated privilege escalation to platform admin via public self-registration
observed_fact: POST /api/auth/register is public and passes caller-supplied role into create_user; ROLES contains admin; handler then issues a live session cookie
preconditions: Network reach to the API. No credentials needed.
user_impact: Total platform compromise
security_impact: Complete auth and authz bypass; defeats all 19 working guards at once
regulatory_impact: SR 11-7 role segregation void; SOX ITGC access provisioning absent; GLBA/GDPR Art.32 failure
reproducibility_impact: Admin can alter any model record
recommendation: Force lowest role server-side in register(); gate public registration behind ATLAS_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION defaulting false
remediation_test: Unauthenticated POST /api/auth/register {"role":"admin"} -> assert created role is data_scientist and GET /api/admin/users with that session is 403

title: Header-asserted identity enabled by default; any client becomes any user without a password
observed_fact: development_user_header_enabled() returns True with no env config; require_user resolves X-ATLAS-USER-ID before the session branch; ATLAS_AUTH_ENABLED=true does not suppress it; enforce_hosted_security_configuration is a no-op unless ATLAS_HOSTED_MODE is true (fail-open)
evidence: security_store.py:26-27,89-92,108-116,582-585; verified live: the entire audit asserted 3 identities with no credentials
user_impact: Impersonation of any user including admins
security_impact: Complete auth bypass; forges audit attribution at the source
regulatory_impact: Audit trail non-repudiation destroyed; SR 11-7/SOX/GLBA/GDPR fail
recommendation: Invert the default: require affirmative ATLAS_ENABLE_DEV_USER_HEADER and default ATLAS_LOCAL_DEV to false; bind to loopback; run the hosted guard unconditionally; strip available_dev_users from 401 bodies
remediation_test: With no env vars set, GET /api/projects with X-ATLAS-USER-ID: <seeded admin> -> assert 401

title: Authenticated users execute arbitrary native code as the server process; =default is not a sandbox
observed_fact: ATLAS_CODE_SANDBOX_COMMAND=default resolves to the project venv interpreter with -I run as a plain child of the API process; no container/seccomp/namespace/rlimit; the authorization guard is conditional on a projectId that defaults to empty; R/SAS/notebook execution routes declare no user at all
preconditions: Any authenticated user plus an operator who set the documented value
user_impact: Read/modify/exfiltrate all users' data and credentials
security_impact: Full server compromise from an authenticated session; enables artifact swap and audit tampering
regulatory_impact: SR 11-7 environment segregation void; PCI-DSS 6.4.1 unmeetable
reproducibility_impact: Any artifact can be silently replaced
recommendation: Make authorization unconditional; add user+scope to R/SAS/notebook routes; rename 'default'; require a real isolation boundary for multi-user deployments
remediation_test: As a non-admin, POST /api/python/run reading the security DB with no projectId -> assert 400/403; POST /api/notebooks/{other user's id}/run-all -> assert 403

title: Cross-user IDOR across ~12 resource families

evidence: Live GET probes this audit; evidence_router.py:95-112; monitoring/router.py; credit_risk_router.py; project_router.py:33; registry/router.py; validation/router.py; notebook_router.py; sql_router.py; dataset_router.py:85-87

evidence: Read-only SQLite query this audit; eval_router.py:271,277-278; result_store.py:23

title: Segregation of duties bypassable via PATCH; approvals not bound to a model version
observed_fact: PATCH /api/validation/cases/{id} with status=approved reaches an approved state without calling approve(), skipping the self-approval check; validation_cases and validation_approvals have no model_version_id; POST /model-versions/{id}/governance-status requires only view permission
user_impact: A model owner can mark their own model approved
regulatory_impact: The most examinable SR 11-7 control - independence of validation - is displayed, partially implemented, and defeated by a documented API on the same router
recommendation: Remove status/final_disposition from CaseUpdateRequest; add an explicit state machine; add model_version_id NOT NULL to cases and approvals; broaden the SoD check to include model owner and version creator; make governance-status internal-only

title: MDD is free-text with no governed identity; the real projection API is dead code; three parallel MDD paths
observed_fact: A real 26-section MDD artifact contains zero occurrences of modelVersionId/datasetVersionId/evidenceId/checksum; championModel is derived by substring-matching a JSON dump; getDocumentationBundle is exported and never called; three persistence paths exist (JSON 2 docs, documentation_packages 0 rows, mdd_* 12 tables 0 rows) and the Registry reads the 0-row one
user_impact: Users hand-write prose and click a button that pastes boilerplate
security_impact: Any authenticated user can read/edit any project's MDD
regulatory_impact: The MDD is the primary examination artifact; today it is unverifiable narrative with no version pins
reproducibility_impact: MDD cannot be regenerated from or checked against lifecycle state
recommendation: Activate the mdd_* schema and retire the other two; every section becomes ordered content blocks that are either resolvable projections or explicitly-marked human text; replace infer_champion_from_text with models.current_version_id; wire getDocumentationBundle; replace str(hash()) with sha256; add authorization
remediation_test: Create project->register version->score->capture evidence->create MDD: assert the MDD contains the exact modelVersionId and evidenceId and that championModel equals the registered algorithm

title: No invalidation: nothing marks documentation/validation/monitoring/evidence stale when upstream changes
observed_fact: Grep for stale|invalidat|supersede returns only in-memory split staleness, an in-memory cache, a manually settable string, and a 90-day wall-clock timer; archive_version explicitly states downstream records are untouched
user_impact: MDD/approval/monitoring continue to display as current with no signal
regulatory_impact: SR 11-7 requires material change to trigger re-review; ATLAS cannot detect material change therefore cannot demonstrate ongoing validity of any approval
reproducibility_impact: A stale MDD asserts facts about data that no longer exists
recommendation: Pin every downstream record to model_version_id; add a computed_over fingerprint; add one lifecycle_invalidation service walking downstream on every version change; surface stale in Registry/Validation/Monitoring and block export on a stale pin
remediation_test: Register v1, create MDD+case+plan bound to v1, register v2 -> assert all three report stale with a reason naming v1->v2 and that export returns 409

title: Artifact checksums never verified on read; joblib.load is an unguarded pickle trust boundary
observed_fact: SHA-256 is computed and stored for model artifacts, scoring parquet and dataset versions and is compared nowhere; load_model_artifact checks path containment and existence then calls joblib.load; scoring_runs and dataset_versions are content-mutable via UPSERT including their checksum columns
evidence: model_artifacts.py:59-60,77-83; scoring_run_artifacts.py:62,80-94; scoring_run_repository.py:83-107; dataset_repository.py:46-73; verified: 186/189 evidence rows have null artifact_hash
preconditions: Filesystem write - which SEC-P0-3 grants to any authenticated user
user_impact: Silent model substitution; all downstream metrics wrong with no indication
security_impact: Chained RCE via unverified pickle deserialization
regulatory_impact: Model inventory integrity unprovable; an institution cannot attest the artifact it scores with is the one validated
reproducibility_impact: Without verified content identity, "the same model" is unfalsifiable
recommendation: Re-hash and compare before deserializing; raise and audit on mismatch; enforce write-once; restrict the UPSERT to lifecycle columns; prefer skops/ONNX or sign the artifact
remediation_test: Tamper one byte on disk -> assert the next load raises ARTIFACT_INTEGRITY_FAILURE and writes an audit row

title: Checkpoint saves failing in production; 923 MB rewritten per request; failure invisible to callers
observed_fact: VERIFIED in uvicorn.err.log: 4 x TypeError('Object of type int64 is not JSON serializable') interleaved with 5 critical-size escalations 236MB->892MB, exactly +163,825,744 bytes per scope; file on disk is 923,653,366 bytes (8.8x the critical threshold); json.dumps has no default= handler; schedule_checkpoint_save returns True unconditionally
preconditions: Any numpy scalar in an unencoded field; any deployment with several resident scopes
user_impact: Silent total loss of all in-progress modeling work on the next restart
regulatory_impact: The only durable path for training results does not exist when this fails; model-risk evidence chains break with no record that loss occurred
scalability_impact: Multi-hundred-MB serialize+write under a lock on every mutating request
recommendation: Route every field through a numpy-aware encoder; serialize per-scope so one bad scope cannot abort the rest; stop storing DataFrames in one JSON - use per-scope Parquet sidecars; make the critical threshold actionable; surface failure on /api/persistence/health
remediation_test: Seed a scope whose target is numpy.int64 -> assert save_checkpoint() is True and round-trips; assert failure appears on the health endpoint

title: Model registry has never persisted a model; failure silently swallowed
observed_fact: VERIFIED: models=0, model_versions=0, artifacts/model_registry does not exist, all 15 scoring runs not_registered; the sole write path is inside except Exception: return None and the caller still returns ok:true
evidence: eval_router.py:240-278,294-301; model_registry_service.py:105-150; live filesystem and SQLite checks
user_impact: User told it saved; after restart RESULTS.final_model is None and the documented fallback has no artifact - scoring permanently broken until retrain
regulatory_impact: No model inventory exists; validators would be shown a registry backed by nothing
recommendation: Remove the blanket except; make create_model_version transactional (artifact temp-write, single DB transaction, then rename); add UNIQUE(model_id, version_number); assert artifact root writability at startup
remediation_test: Save final model -> assert a row and a model.joblib exist, or a non-2xx with an explicit error; assert scoring after restart loads from the registry artifact

title: Two divergent audit trails; ~3900 events in only one; second write is except: pass
observed_fact: VERIFIED: audit_events=9136 in the security DB vs audit_log=5466 in the app DB; the second write is wrapped in except Exception: pass after the first connection is already committed
preconditions: Any period of persistence unavailability or any process writing one DB only
user_impact: Admin audit views show materially different histories; neither is complete
regulatory_impact: An audit trail that is silently lossy and internally contradictory fails SOX, SR 11-7 and GDPR Art.30 completeness expectations; except: pass on an audit write is itself a control failure
recommendation: Choose one authoritative audit store; if both must exist use an outbox in the first DB with a retrying drain; never swallow an audit-write failure; add a reconciliation report run at startup and in CI
remediation_test: Inject a persistence failure -> assert either both stores have the row or the caller sees an error; assert a reconciliation report shows zero divergence

title: Evidence split across three stores that have already diverged; JSON evidence API has no authorization
observed_fact: 227 JSON index entries / 203 item files / 189 SQLite rows with only ~126 IDs common; 53 index rows with no file; 29 files not indexed; evidence_router performs no authorization on any handler; write_json is a naive in-place truncate
preconditions: Any authenticated session; any crash or concurrent write
user_impact: Evidence listed in the UI 404s on open; evidence that exists is invisible; one user can delete another's evidence
security_impact: Cross-tenant read and delete confirmed live
regulatory_impact: Evidence is the substrate of documentation and validation; a tamper-accessible lossy unreconciled store cannot support a validation submission
reproducibility_impact: Coverage scores computed from an index that does not match reality
recommendation: Consolidate on the SQLite table with content-addressed payload files; make write_json atomic with a unique temp name and a lock; add authorization to every handler; add project-deletion cleanup and a startup orphan report
remediation_test: Crash/concurrency test asserting index and files stay consistent; assert a stranger gets 403/404 on list/read/update/delete

title: New project inherits the previous project's step-completion marks

evidence: useWorkflowStore.ts:163-171,181,261-279,287; screenshot 002-da-03 renders 1 of 14 steps / 7% on a project whose every scope tile reads Not selected
preconditions: Create a project after completing a step in another
user_impact: Analyst believes a step is done on a project where it was never opened and skips it
regulatory_impact: The progress bar and the Step 11 readiness % are the completion attestation a reviewer reads; asserting Data Acquisition complete on a project with no dataset is a false control attestation
reproducibility_impact: Completion record does not reflect work performed
recommendation: Delete the legacy steps record (shadow state for workflowSteps) or reset it inside startProjectFromWorkflow and stop passing state.steps into both merge helpers
remediation_test: Complete /step01 in A, create B -> assert every workflowSteps status is pending and the header reads 0 of 14

title: Project Context leaks into a new project and is autosaved into it
observed_fact: The form hydrates from the global unscoped key modeling-tool-project-context; when the backend has no context and no project draft exists the autosave hook's else branch never calls onHydrated, so the prior narrative remains and the first keystroke writes it to the new project's backend record
preconditions: Create a project after filling Project Context in another
user_impact: Project B created carrying Project A's business objective and target definition
regulatory_impact: Intended-use, target and population statements are what a validator maps to the model's approved use; silent contamination could cause approval against another model's use boundary
reproducibility_impact: Governance narrative attributed to the wrong model
recommendation: Hydrate from defaults not loadProjectContext(); call onHydrated in the else branch; block editing until hydrated; migrate the 18 readers to the project-scoped path
remediation_test: Fill A's context, create B -> assert every field is default and that B's backend record contains no A string after typing

title: Data Acquisition renders a second contradicting readiness derivation in the milestone panel
observed_fact: resolveStageStates returns complete for all seven stages from progress.phase === loaded, including Evaluating data quality and Ready for modeling; the producer performs no quality work between advance(4) and advance(5)
evidence: dataAcquisitionLifecycle.ts:298-306,334-348; Step01_DataAcquisition.tsx:1474-1491,1509; screenshot 003-ui-03 shows 7 of 7 milestones and Ready for modeling COMPLETE beside Modeling Readiness Not evaluated and Quality profiling has not been generated

regulatory_impact: A screenshot-able assertion that a data-quality control executed when it did not; qualifies the prior phase's completion claim
recommendation: Make the milestone track a projection of deriveDataAcquisitionStatus; stages 3-6 read governedProfile.phase and stage 7 reads readiness; remove the blanket loaded->complete shortcut
remediation_test: Before the profile resolves assert the milestone count is not 7 of 7 while the readiness badge reads Not evaluated

title: Evaluation silently substitutes another project's model metrics
observed_fact: On an empty governed response and on any backend failure Step 8 falls back to loadLocalRanked(), which reads the global project-unscoped sessionStorage key modeling-tool-training-summary
preconditions: Open project A with trained models then project B without
user_impact: Project B's Evaluation Command Center displays Project A's AUC/PR-AUC/RMSE
regulatory_impact: Champion-model selection evidence attributed to the wrong model; if exported to the MDD this is a direct misstatement of performance to a validator
reproducibility_impact: Metrics attributed to the wrong model
recommendation: Delete the fallback; an empty governed response renders an explicit empty state and a backend failure renders the failure - matching the no-fallback invariant already enforced in governedProfile.ts
remediation_test: Train in A, switch to B, stub /train/last empty -> assert zero model rows and no A model key in the DOM

title: Sign-out leaves all governed browser state readable by the next user
observed_fact: logout() clears only atlas:modeling-dataset:* in sessionStorage; every localStorage key survives including project context, EDA commentary, the decision journal, bureau treatments and user Python/SAS
user_impact: Next user sees the prior user's project context and decision journal
regulatory_impact: Breaks per-user attribution of the decision journal (the override audit trail); bureau treatments are FCRA/ECOA-relevant
recommendation: Add clearUserLocalState() sweeping every modeling-tool-* and atlas:*-draft key on logout and call it before dropping the cached identity
remediation_test: Sign in as A, complete steps, sign out, sign in as B -> assert no modeling-tool-* key exists

title: No error boundary is mounted anywhere

user_impact: Whole application white-screens; unsaved narrative in Steps 12/13 is lost with it

remediation_test: Inject a throwing child into /step09 -> assert the shell still renders and a recovery action is present

title: Large fraction of the Node suite asserts on source text not behaviour
observed_fact: Main-agent measurement: 20 of 54 files use readFileSync with no execution mechanism; the testing lane counted 31 of 54 with broader criteria; ~2008 assert.match calls across 43 files; zero .test.mjs files import from src/

title: No CI exists; the documented release gate runs 1 of 66 scripts
observed_fact: VERIFIED: git ls-files matching .github/, gitlab-ci, Jenkinsfile, azure-pipelines, .circleci returns 0; there is no npm test aggregate script; RELEASE_CHECKLIST runs only test:experimental-design

title: A clean install produces an environment that has never been tested
observed_fact: Two requirements files disagree on 6 of 17 overlapping packages and the venv is a mixture of both; 26 of 51 declared packages are not installed including pytest; 7 drift; duckdb/polars/pyarrow appear in neither file and polars/pyarrow are module-scope imports at boot

security_impact: Unused python-jose and psycopg2-binary declarations generate false SCA findings
regulatory_impact: A regulator asking to reproduce the validation environment cannot be answered; ydata-profiling raises a commercial-licence question for a bank
reproducibility_impact: Every test result was produced against an environment no file describes

remediation_test: Clean container: pip install -r requirements.lock, pip check, assert pip freeze diff is empty, run the full Python suite

title: The 16 highest-value behavioral tests are orphaned and never run
observed_fact: None of the 16 filenames appears in any of the 66 package.json scripts; they include every two-user authorization test, the segregation-of-duties test, the lockout test, the checkpoint-GC test and both independent statistical-reference tests
user_impact: None directly
security_impact: The controls a bank cares about most are verified by excellent tests no process executes
regulatory_impact: Zero ongoing assurance for isolation and four-eyes approval
reproducibility_impact: Proof of consequence: checkpoint_lifecycle_test.py was written to prevent the checkpoint defect that is now recurring at 2.9x scale

title: Cross-resource substitution: project_id and dataset_id validated independently never for coherence
observed_fact: run_python authorizes projectId and separately authorizes context.datasetId but never checks the dataset is linked to that project; the correct both-sides pattern exists at dataset_router.py:201-205; PUT /api/evidence/{id} accepts an arbitrary projectId and re-parents freely while persistence_router.py:405-408 forbids exactly that
preconditions: One session plus any dataset the caller can view
user_impact: Another tenant's model or evidence becomes attached to the attacker's project
security_impact: Integrity violation of the resource graph
regulatory_impact: Model inventory and lineage integrity (SR 11-7 SectionV, BCBS 239); a documentation package citing an unauthorized dataset is a material misstatement
recommendation: Introduce authorize_resource_in_project(user, project_id, type, id) asserting the resource's stored project_id equals the supplied one; forbid re-parenting in PUT /api/evidence
remediation_test: As B, POST /api/python/run with projectId=projB and datasetId=dsA -> assert 403

title: Session cookie not Secure by default; no CSRF token anywhere
observed_fact: secure = not ATLAS_LOCAL_DEV or ATLAS_HOSTED_MODE evaluates to False with defaults; no CSRF token, double-submit or Origin check exists; CORS uses allow_credentials with allow_headers=[*] so X-ATLAS-USER-ID is accepted cross-origin
preconditions: Network-adjacent attacker on any non-TLS hop
user_impact: Session theft
security_impact: SameSite=Lax incidentally mitigates the cookie path and gives zero protection on the header path
regulatory_impact: PCI-DSS 4.1 / GLBA transmission security; SOC 2 CC6.7
recommendation: Set secure=True unless an explicit insecure opt-in is present; add a CSRF token for state-changing routes; replace allow_headers=[*] with an explicit list excluding X-ATLAS-USER-ID
remediation_test: Assert Set-Cookie contains Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax with no env vars set

title: No per-user resource quotas
observed_fact: Per-request bounds are good but nothing limits concurrent /python/run subprocesses per caller and subprocess.run sets no memory or child-process rlimit; several limit params are unclamped while the correct pattern exists at registry/router.py:34
preconditions: One session and N concurrent requests
user_impact: Platform-wide unavailability for all tenants
regulatory_impact: SOC 2 A1.1 availability
recommendation: Add a per-user concurrency semaphore reusing analytics/resource_governance; apply Query(default, ge, le) to every limit; add rlimits to the execution subprocess
remediation_test: Fire 50 concurrent /python/run as one user -> assert 429 beyond the cap and that /api/health still responds

title: random_seed recorded but never used - the persisted training contract is materially false
observed_fact: TrainingJobRequest.random_seed is recorded into the contract and the summary; train_models() has no seed parameter and is never passed one; 29 sites hardcode random_state=42; the split path does honour the seed, creating an inconsistency
evidence: training_job_service.py:194,427-438; trainer.py:1268-1279 and 29 random_state=42 sites; split_router.py:26,181
preconditions: Any training run with a non-default seed
user_impact: A user changing the seed to test stability gets bit-identical results and concludes the model is seed-insensitive
regulatory_impact: The persisted training contract is materially false; sensitivity-to-seed analysis (a standard validation test) is impossible
reproducibility_impact: Superficially benign but the record is wrong, which is worse than a missing field
recommendation: Thread random_seed through train_models to every factory, StratifiedKFold and the SHAP subsample; copy the resolved seed into training_parameters_json
remediation_test: Train with seed 1 and seed 2 -> assert fitted coefficients differ; twice with seed 1 -> assert identical

title: Evidence mutable hard-deletable silently overwritten and unattributed
observed_fact: evidence_id_for derives the id from mutable descriptive fields so re-running an analysis silently overwrites prior evidence with no history; PUT merges arbitrary fields; DELETE hard-unlinks with no tombstone and no audit event; 184 of 203 live items have createdBy=ATLAS
preconditions: Any re-run or any authenticated user
user_impact: Evidence a user believed captured is silently replaced
security_impact: Cross-project write and delete confirmed live
regulatory_impact: Evidence must be append-only, attributable and tamper-evident; any evidence pack exported from this store is unreliable
reproducibility_impact: Historical record of what was observed and when is not retained
recommendation: Make evidence append-only with content-addressed ids and supersedes links; replace DELETE with retire; restrict PUT to annotative fields; set createdBy server-side; emit audit events
remediation_test: Capture E1, re-capture identical -> assert E2 exists with supersedes=E1 and E1 still readable; DELETE returns 405

title: governed_version/workspace_draft enforced at exactly one endpoint
observed_fact: require_evidence_eligible has exactly two grep hits: its definition and one call site in target_intelligence_router; POST /api/evidence performs no scope check and normalize_item never inspects analysisScope; it auto-promotes to ready on a client-satisfiable quality score; 185 of 203 live items carry no scope
preconditions: Any evidence capture outside Target Intelligence
user_impact: An unregistered workspace analysis appears in the Evidence Graph indistinguishable from a version-pinned one
regulatory_impact: The module's own preamble describes exactly the defect that remains open on 91% of live evidence
reproducibility_impact: Draft evidence is not reproducible and is indistinguishable from governed
recommendation: Make analysisScope required; call require_evidence_eligible inside upsert_evidence (one enforcement point not per-router); reject client-supplied eligibility; remove the quality-score auto-promotion
remediation_test: Compute over an unregistered frame -> assert POST /evidence returns 409 naming the workspace-draft reason

title: Monitoring unbound to any model version hand-keyed unauthorized and unorchestrated
observed_fact: monitoring_plans and monitoring_baselines carry project_id only with no model reference; record_observation reads observed_value from the body with no role check and never reads scoring_runs.psi_json/vsi_json which are populated; no scheduler exists; next_reviews_due counts any plan with a date set
user_impact: Monitoring is a manual form; users type numbers ATLAS already computed
regulatory_impact: Ongoing monitoring is an explicit SR 11-7 requirement tied to the approved model version; a baseline with no model binding cannot detect that the model changed; absent orchestration there is no evidence monitoring occurred at the stated cadence
recommendation: Add model_version_id NOT NULL to plans and baselines; derive metric summaries server-side from the pinned version; add scoring_run_id to observations; add role checks and project authorization; add a scheduler; fix next_reviews_due
remediation_test: Create a plan without model_version_id -> 422; post an observation as an ungranted user -> 403; assert observed_value is server-derived

title: No reproducibility envelope
observed_fact: A model_versions row captures algorithm, a class name mislabeled algorithm_version, grid-search best params, metrics and an artifact path; it does not capture Python or library versions, environment identity, target class mapping, split row indices, feature order, default hyperparameters or code identity; environment_inventory computes exactly this and is called only by the Python code panel
user_impact: Users cannot answer what exactly produced this model
regulatory_impact: SR 11-7 requires development documented in sufficient detail for an independent party to reconstruct it; ATLAS captures roughly a quarter of the envelope; LabelEncoder is fit over train+test which is itself a defect a validator should flag

title: No backup restore retention RPO/RTO rollback or DR story
observed_fact: No backup script (only a pre-reset copy that captures atlas_local.db without WAL sidecars the security DB artifacts or the checkpoint); no restore procedure; zero occurrences of RPO or RTO in docs; 15 forward-only migrations with no down path; the documented backup is a developer's local folder sync
user_impact: No recovery; RPO unbounded and RTO undefined

recommendation: Add a backup script using SQLite's online-backup API for both DBs plus an artifact and checkpoint snapshot with a manifest and checksums; add a restore script with a verification pass; document RPO/RTO; implement retention and an orphan sweeper; author down-migrations

title: No concurrency job-recovery or reproducibility tests
